cards.front: Recall a key point about The Marketing Mix
cards.back: The marketing mix (4Ps) combines Product, Price, Place, and Promotion into a coherent strategy. All elements must be consistent - a premium product at a budget price with limited availability and cheap advertising creates confusion.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Marketing Mix
cards.back: Product: what is being sold, including features, quality, design, branding, packaging, and after-sales service. It must meet customer needs and be differentiated from competitors.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Marketing Mix
cards.back: Price: must reflect the product's positioning and target market's willingness to pay. Premium products need premium prices; budget products need competitive prices. Pricing must also cover costs and generate profit.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Marketing Mix
cards.back: Place: how and where the product is sold. Luxury goods are sold in exclusive outlets; everyday products need wide distribution. Online channels have changed place strategy for most businesses.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Marketing Mix
cards.back: Promotion: how customers learn about the product. Must reach the target market through appropriate channels and communicate the right message aligned with the product's positioning.

cards.front: What should you know about business exam tips?
cards.back: When evaluating the marketing mix, use the CCC framework: Consistency (do all 4Ps send the same message?), Customer focus (does the mix serve the target market's needs?), Competitive advantage (does the mix differentiate from rivals?). A strong marketing mix is coherent, customer-centred, and competitive.

Students often make mistakes here. Wrong: A good product will sell itself, so the other 3Ps don't matter as much. Correct: Even the best product will fail without the right marketing mix support. A brilliant product at the wrong price (too high for the market), unavailable in the right places, or unknown to the target customers will not sell. cards.front: Assessment Objective Focus: The Marketing Mix
cards.back: AO1 — Knowledge: Demonstrate knowledge of The Marketing Mix with precise business/economic terminology. Define key terms and state accurate factual information.

cards.front: Understanding The Marketing Mix in Business Context
cards.back: The Marketing Mix is a key topic in GCSE Business Studies that affects how businesses operate in the UK economy. Understanding this concept requires knowledge of both theoretical principles and real-world application. The AQA specification requires you to explain, analyse and evaluate business concepts using appropriate terminology, and apply them to real business scenarios using UK examples.

cards.front: Applying The Marketing Mix to UK Business Examples
cards.back: For the marketing mix, applying theory to practice means using real UK business examples to illustrate your understanding. Small businesses face different challenges from large corporations when dealing with the marketing mix. Consider how factors like business size, ownership structure, industry sector and market position affect the impact of the marketing mix on a business.

cards.front: Exam Technique for The Marketing Mix Questions
cards.back: GCSE Business exam questions about the marketing mix range from 1-mark definition questions to 12-mark evaluation questions. For definition questions (1-2 marks), give a precise business definition. For explanation questions (3-4 marks), define and explain with a brief example.
